root: ^Fishwife: Fish! Fresh from the nets — none of that slimy rot the others try to pawn off.

c-0: ^Fishwife: Trout, perch, pike — all fat and clean. Fresher than morning dew, caught just hours ago.
^ I’ve got fillets for your pan, whole fish for your stew, and even a few river eels if you fancy something different.
^Fishwife: Fair coin for fair catch. I don’t cheat my customers — you’ll get what you pay for, and not a scale less.
c-1: ^Fishwife: If you want my advice, try the perch. Sweet flesh, easy bones. Perfect for supper.
^Fishwife: I grew up on the docks, learning the trade from my parents. My father showed me how to cast nets, my mother how to clean a catch.
^ It’s hard work—long days, rough weather, and sometimes danger. I’ve seen storms take boats and friends alike.
^ The sea’s cruel… but it keeps you honest.
c-2: ^Fishwife: Aye, I’ve heard talk. The butcher dyes spoiled meat with berries to hide the black. Fools still buy it. I wouldn’t feed it to a dog.
